commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

The decodeBlock() resize was dead code: every tagDecoder() branch that
needs more than the box header now allocates its own buffer, so growing
the shared 5-byte header buffer to the full box size achieved nothing.
Drop it.

While here, trim the Nikon NCTG scratch buffer to the 200-byte maximum the
decoder documents and sanity-checks against; the trailing byte was unused.

(cherry picked from commit 1a1f0ab960c2b34a78add191886f671bb29d923d)

Nul-terminate strings

Several of the QuickTime decoders copied fixed-width atom payloads into a
DataBuf and then handed buf.data() straight to a std::string, relying on
whatever happened to follow in the buffer to terminate it. Allocate one
extra byte and write an explicit '\0' after the payload instead.

Also express the Nikon NCTG string-length guard against the documented
200-byte maximum directly, the same way the sibling dataType branches
already do (dataLength > 200), rather than phrasing it in terms of the
buffer's allocation size.

(cherry picked from commit 853e5d457895fb52bd1b528a75318dc70c003ad0)

coupling: The defect is the broken N+1 'payload + trailing NUL slot' invariant of the Nikon NCTG string buffer in QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder, split across the two commits so no single diff is wrong. In the original code the scratch buffer is DataBuf buf(201) and the dataType==2/7 branch processes an entry only when `dataLength >= buf.size()` (i.e. dataLength <= 200), then reads `dataLength` bytes and writes the terminator with `buf.data()[dataLength] = '\0'` (a raw, unchecked pointer write) at index at most 200 -- the 201st byte, which is exactly the slack the 201-size buffer provides. Commit 1421cf3 ('Remove unnecessary resize') trims buf(201) to buf(200), framed as dropping an unused byte; on its own this is safe because the guard is still `>= buf.size()`, which now self-adjusts to cap dataLength at 199, so the terminator lands at index <=199 (in-bounds for a 200-byte buffer). Commit 119dadc ('Nul-terminate strings') rewrites the same guard from `>= buf.size()` to the explicit `> 200`, framed as matching the sibling dataType 3/4/5/8 branches that already use `> 200`; on its own this is safe because at that point the buffer is still 201 bytes, so dataLength up to 200 writes the terminator at index 200 (in-bounds for 201). Only the composition is unsafe: buffer size 200 AND a guard that allows dataLength==200 lets `buf.data()[200] = '\0'` write one byte past the end of the 200-byte heap allocation (CWE-787). A correct fix must reason across both commits -- it has to re-couple the guard bound to the real allocation size (e.g. restore the `+1` slack byte, or make the guard `>= buf.size()` / `>= 200` again). Reviewing either commit's diff in isolation reveals nothing: the buffer allocation (line 920) and the guard+terminator write (lines 1041/1050) are ~130 lines apart and only one of them appears in each commit's hunk, so neither per-commit diff exposes the mismatch. Verified by build+run: base main clean; original batch clean; buf(200)-only (1421cf3 edit alone) clean; guard>200-only (119dadc edit alone) clean; both edits together abort under AddressSanitizer with a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow write at quicktimevideo.cpp:1050.
